html:
Louisiana was the French colony in the Mississippi basin, part of New France. The map shows its small settled core on the Gulf coast around Mobile and Biloxi in 1715.

René Robert Cavelier de La Salle canoed down the Mississippi River in 1682 and claimed its whole basin for Louis XIV, naming it after him. Pierre Le Moyne d'Iberville founded the first settlements at Biloxi in 1699 and Mobile in 1702. The colony relied on alliances with Native nations, above all the Choctaw.

In 1717 the Scottish financier John Law's Mississippi Company took over the colony, founded New Orleans in 1718 and brought in settlers and enslaved Africans, before its bubble burst in 1720. Louisiana never made France much money. After the Seven Years' War France gave the land west of the Mississippi and New Orleans to Spain in 1762, and the east to Britain in 1763. It became Spanish Luisiana.
